summary: At 3,842 square miles, Shasta County is larger than Delaware and Rhode Island combined, yet holds fewer than 200,000 people — a density of just 47 per square mile that translates to vast stretches of pine forest, volcanic terrain, and open rangeland between small towns. Mount Shasta's 14,179-foot peak anchors the northern horizon, Whiskeytown Lake and Shasta Lake (California's largest reservoir) provide hundreds of miles of shoreline, and the Sacramento River threads right through Redding, the county seat and economic center where Mercy Medical Center and Shasta Regional Medical Center are major employers alongside government and retail — healthcare and the public sector effectively are the job market here, which means switching employers without relocating is possible but the pool is shallow. A median home price of $347,200 against a median household income of roughly $72,000 yields a price-to-income ratio near 4.8, noticeably more accessible than coastal California, though a 13% poverty rate suggests that affordability is relative to which rung of the local economy you occupy. Summers are hot and emphatically sunny — 8.9 hours of daily sunshine year-round — while winters bring cool nights averaging in the mid-30s and occasional snow at elevation. The tradeoff that defines Shasta County is geographic grandeur paired with economic narrowness: extraordinary natural infrastructure, limited professional infrastructure.
